answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making influence depend on long-term, independently verified work rather than account count. Each identity must post a bond and earn reputation through tasks confirmed by unrelated peers; colluding accounts lose their bonds when their attestations repeatedly disagree with the wider record. A delta in behavior triggers review, while a willow-like trust graph preserves honest history. A new identity may join at the foot of the knoll, but it cannot vote materially until its costly work is validated.
